campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council agenda for October 6, 2026, lists discussion of temporary legal services arrangements during the transition to a new city attorney. It also includes items on compensation and working conditions for certain unrepresented employee groups, and a proposed market-based salary adjustment for the city manager.
keyTopics: Temporary legal services during the city attorney transition
Compensation and working conditions for unrepresented confidential, classified management, and unclassified management employees
Market adjustment to the city manager's salary

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's October 7, 2026, agenda listed routine business such as meeting minutes, check registers, and a Treasurer's Report, alongside several substantive items. These include a $2.5 million budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project, a new no-parking zone on Chester Avenue, a decision on the city's long-term law enforcement provider, a comparison of animal care service providers, and a public hearing on annual code updates.
keyTopics: Budget amendment adding $2,500,000 for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project
Proposed No Parking Anytime zone on both sides of Chester Avenue near Arcadia Palms Drive
Discussion and determination of the city's long-term law enforcement provider, including a possible agreement with Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
Comparison of regional animal care providers, including whether to continue with San Jose Animal Care and Services
Public hearing on annual code updates covering appeal scheduling, City Commissioner qualifications, and business record retention

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 13, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council's agenda for October 13, 2026, lists several routine financial and project approval items, along with resolutions on a residential electrification rebate program and updated Below Market Rate housing guidelines. The agenda also includes a review of the Commission and Committee Handbook and an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center.
keyTopics: Resolution to appropriate $78,000 from the general fund for a residential electrification rebate program
Resolution approving updated Below Market Rate (BMR) For-Sale and Rental Housing Guidelines, with a CEQA determination that the action is exempt under Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3)
Resolutions accepting completion of two public works projects: sanitary sewer spot repairs/CCTV inspections and the FY 2024-2025 Annual Streets Project by O'Grady Paving
Adoption of an updated Conflict of Interest Code for staff and commissioners
Review of the Commission and Committee Handbook, with possible direction on revisions

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's October 6, 2026, agenda listed routine business, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and accounts payable reports. It also included a bid issue with a tree services contractor, an update to the Finance Commission's work plan, a proposed change to the Town's purchasing policy, and the July 2026 expenditure and revenue reports.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First Amendment to an agreement authorized for execution by the Town Manager
Finance Commission's updated 2026 work plan
Resolution amending the Town of Los Gatos Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 expenditure and revenue reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 14, 2026
san-jose.summary: This is the San José Rules and Open Government Committee's agenda-planning meeting, where members review and adjust the upcoming October 20 and October 27, 2026, City Council agendas. The agenda also includes a review of recent public records, a District 9 funding request for the Rotary Club of San Jose Foundation, and a retroactive travel/absence approval.
keyTopics: Review and adjustment of the October 20, 2026 final Council agenda
Review and adjustment of the October 27, 2026 draft Council agenda
Public record review covering October 1-8, 2026
District 9 SAP funding request for the Rotary Club of San Jose Foundation
Retroactive approval of travel and an excused absence for a Council member

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee — October 15, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for this Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee meeting is an open format where city staff will be present to answer questions from residents about their neighborhoods. Residents were invited to submit questions in advance online, and the agenda also includes standard procedural notices about accessibility and public comment.
keyTopics: City staff available to answer neighborhood-related questions from residents
Option for residents to submit questions in advance online

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council's October 6, 2026, agenda listed several routine approvals (meeting minutes, claims and bills, and a consulting contract amendment for environmental services at the SMaRT Station and landfill), along with recognitions for Little League All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, and Friends of the Library Week. The agenda also included public hearings on restricting potable water use for nonfunctional turf irrigation, a proposed Service Worker Retention Ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: Public hearing and proposed ordinance to prohibit potable water irrigation of nonfunctional turf under AB 1572
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation
Amendment to a WSP USA Inc. consulting agreement for environmental services at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill, increasing funding and extending the contract through 2028
Easement negotiation with PG&E over a portion of the Clean Water Facility

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — October 14, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission's agenda for October 14, 2026, lists a presentation on Silicon Valley Clean Energy's education sponsorship program, a cybersecurity awareness item, and a spotlight on the youth-led group Food Lifts. The agenda also includes approval of September minutes and selection of the 2026-2027 Chair and Vice Chair.
keyTopics: Silicon Valley Clean Energy education sponsorship program
Cybersecurity awareness
Youth-led organization Food Lifts featured in the Teen Commission Highlight Program
Selection of 2026-2027 Chair and Vice Chair
Approval of September 9, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Neighborhood-University Relations Committee — October 19, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara Neighborhood-University Relations Committee has a special meeting agenda for October 19, 2026, covering approval of past meeting minutes, next year's meeting calendar, and a discussion about nuisance issues tied to private property leases in the Old Quad neighborhood near Santa Clara University. The agenda also lists update reports from the Community Development Department, Santa Clara University, and the Police Department.
keyTopics: Approval of NURC meeting minutes from May 18, 2026
Adoption of the 2027 Neighborhood University Relations Committee meeting calendar
Discussion of neighborhood nuisance issues in private property leases, with possible direction to staff on communicating committee input to property owners in the Old Quad neighborhood
Update reports from the Community Development Department, Santa Clara University, and the Police Department

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council's agenda for this meeting covers several financial and infrastructure topics, including federal housing grant funding, a traffic camera safety program, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The agenda also lists bond refunding actions tied to the former Redevelopment Agency's successor agency.
keyTopics: Approval of the Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency regarding bond matters
Resolution authorizing the sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Architectural Review Board's agenda for this meeting lists a public hearing on an AT&T application to add new antennas and related equipment to existing city-owned wood utility poles near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue. The agenda marks the proposal as exempt from environmental review under CEQA's existing facilities exemption, and notes a supplemental report and draft materials were added for the item.
keyTopics: AT&T request to collocate two Tier 2 wireless facilities (antennas, remote radio units, seven-foot pole extensions) on city utility poles near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Item classified as a quasi-judicial public hearing (26PLN-00229)
CEQA exemption determination under Guideline Section 15301 (Existing Facilities)
Supplemental report and draft architectural review materials added to the agenda item
